title: Labeling Old Family Photographs
description: Add names and dates to photographs while the people are remembered.
cardDescription: Add names and dates to photographs while the people are remembered.
focus: The setting is labeling Old Family Photographs. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Day and month on a calendar
Book used to hold a set of photographs
Calendar period divided into twelve months
Image made with a camera or pencil

answerNotes.PHOTO: Photo is short for photograph. A caption or name label can preserve information that the image alone does not supply.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.
answerNotes.FACE: Face can name the front of a head or the marked surface of a clock. The surrounding objects identify the sense used in the clue.

answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.

answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.PARENT: A parent is a mother or father. Family stories and trees can include parents by birth, adoption, or other family relationships.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Object preserved as a reminder of a person or event
Words formed with a pen or pencil
Identifying word beside a family photograph
Material used for writing or wrapping

answerNotes.LETTER: Letter can mean a written message or one alphabet character. An envelope clue points to the message sense.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
